messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden spike in 5xx from gateway cluster in us-east-2 (egress stage). 2-minute p95 5xx rate = 9.8% (baseline ~0.2%). Auto-escalation: paging oncall. links: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/5161712345 :rotating_light:

sam-oncall: I'm on it. seeing a surge in 502/504 from the us-east-2 edge pool. customers showing increased latencies. paging @ravi-runtime and @jamie-infra.

ravi-runtime: copy. pulling gateway logs now. any top-customer hits or is it broad?

jamie-infra: infra dashboard shows high connection churn on the frontage NLB in eastus2 and target group healthy hosts dropping to 60%. could be backend worker saturation or a memory leak.

kyle-sre: corroborating traces — requests start failing at gateway->egress-proxy with `upstream reset` and intermittent TLS handshake timeouts. redis request cache latency normal.

sam-oncall: customer-impact: a handful of high-traffic customers (~4 customers) are getting a lot of timeouts; broad user-facing errors for some PLG apps. Severity: potential S2 -> S1 if it continues.

ravi-runtime: can we drain the problematic edgepool and shift traffic to us-east-1 and us-west-2? what's our current cross-region failover runbook?

jamie-infra: we have a routing policy to steer 30% traffic away from degraded pools. I can increase to 80% while we investigate. doing a careful steer to avoid overloading other regions.

sam-oncall: do it. prefer gradual to avoid ripple. jamie please post the command you run.

jamie-infra: running:
```
./route-shift --from eastus2 --to [use1,usw2] --percent 80 --auth-token $ROUTE_KEY
```
Starting at 5161712400 - watching for load in targets.

incident-bot: NOTE: traffic shift initiated by jamie-infra. expected near-term reduction in eastus2 qps; monitor for increased 5xx in target regions.

kyle-sre: after initial 30% shift we see eastus2 5xx drop to 5.2% and target regions healthy. after 80% shift eastus2 5xx down to 0.8% — suggests localized capacity/egress issue.

ravi-runtime: capturing core logs from one of the failing gateway hosts. found repeated `worker OOM` messages and `segfault` on ml-proxy process. attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:32Z] ml-proxy[pid:21421] ERROR: oom-killer invoked, rescued processes: [ml-proxy, grpc-thread]
[2026-03-15T10:12:32Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 21421 (ml-proxy) score 987
```
This looks like a regression in a recent runtime rollout.

sam-oncall: which canary/coderev rolled to eastus2 recently?

ravi-runtime: rollout id `ml-proxy-2026-03-15-6b2f` went to canary then auto-rolled. can we pin eastus2 to previous revision while we rollback?

jamie-infra: can pin. running:
```
kubectl set image deployment/ml-proxy ml-proxy=registry/redwood/ml-proxy:2026-03-01-9a1b --namespace=edge-eastus2
```
Initiated at 5161712485.

incident-bot: ACTION: automatic fallback to previous ml-proxy image requested by jamie-infra.

kyle-sre: after pinning, OOM events stop on restarted pods. eastus2 gateway 5xx falls below 0.5% over 2 mins. good signal rollback fixed runtime regression.

lexi-product: quick note for customers: which segments were affected? SDK traffic? API?

cs-ops: primary impact was generating endpoints and high-concurrency SDK usage from a few enterprise customers; embeddings/async batch jobs unaffected. we're drafting a short incident note for affected tenants.

sam-oncall: assigning incident severity S2 -> downgraded to S3 (no longer widespread) but keep incident open for postmortem and release rollback follow-up. sam-oncall -> ravi-runtime handoff to lead the postmortem.

ravi-runtime: taking lead. immediate next steps: 1) runbook-run to capture root cause, 2) block the faulty image from other regions, 3) run integration stress tests against ml-proxy to reproduce OOM locally, 4) communicate with CS for customer comms.

jamie-infra: notes: route-shift rollback not necessary; left at 80% for 10min to ensure no latent errors while we verify. I'll return traffic to normal at +30m if no regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: initial cause = runtime regression (ml-proxy OOM) in eastus2. mitigation = rollback to previous image + traffic steer. Status = under control. Postmortem owner = ravi-runtime.

sam-oncall: thanks team. please add any relevant logs/links to the ticket: https://incidents.redwood/5161712345. we'll schedule blameless postmortem and customer outreach. :white_check_mark:
